title: A finitely generated group with no nontrivial amenable quotient acting vertex-freely on a bounded-valence hyperbolic graph
source_title: A non-residually finite group acting uniformly properly on a hyperbolic space
author: Rémi Coulon; Denis Osin
difficulty_reason: The authors must preserve a uniformly proper bounded-geometry hyperbolic action under the particular high-power fillings, using their complete cylinder-overlap and cone-metric comparison constructions. They then build noncommensurable elements that are conjugate in every finite quotient through an explicit characteristic-core argument inside the Rips kernel. The distinct-prime quotient and property(T) closing uses that new geometric and finite-quotient mechanism to kill all amenable quotients while retaining a non-trivial action; the packet includes the full authored obligations rather than only citing the small-cancellation foundation.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Existence theorem1.1: G is finitely generated and nontrivial, acts isometrically on a Gromov-hyperbolic graph of uniformly bounded valence, freely on its VERTEX SET, and every amenable quotient is trivial. In particular it is not residually finite. Full2.1 uniform cylinder overlap,3.3 separated-orbit graph construction and explicit valence bound,4.2 both cone-metric comparison regimes,4.4 rescaled small-cancellation quotient stability,5.1 finite characteristic-core conjugacy argument and5.2 distinct-prime property(T) construction read. Coulon geometric small-cancellation theorem4.3 is stated with all four conclusions; torsion-free hyperbolic property(T) groups, common hyperbolic quotients and Belegradek–Osin Rips construction are stated advanced foundations. New bounded-geometry quotient control and finite-quotient conjugacy mechanism are printed. Source4.4(1) writes E(g_i)/<g_i> although the displayed filling familyQ uses <g_i^(n_i)> and the final proof explicitly takes ordern_i: theorem4.3(2) for that very family gives the latter quotient, fixing the local denominator notation. No author mathematics altered or replacement proof supplied. The selected theorem is not a claim that an infinite hyperbolic group itself has no finite quotients, nor that the action is cocompact or the group finitely presented. No standalone closure proposition or other torsion-order parameter unit counted.
